question: What is the main goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To provide free meals for the entire local community
options.B: To protect and promote the well-being of students and staff
options.C: To replace the need for community primary healthcare centers
options.D: To train students to become professional healthcare workers

explanation: You got this! The core aim is simply to safeguard the physical, mental, and social health of everyone inside the school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why are schools considered great spots for public health interventions?

options.A: Schools have unlimited financial resources to buy medical equipment
options.B: Teachers possess advanced clinical degrees in nursing and medicine
options.C: Students are legally required to receive medical treatment at school
options.D: Children spend a large portion of their formative years gathered in one place

explanation: Spot on! When children are gathered in one learning spot, public health workers can easily reach many of them at once to build healthy habits. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which of these belongs to the physical school environment?

options.A: The academic grading scale used by teachers
options.B: Safe drinking water and functional sanitation
options.C: The political affiliation of the local school board
options.D: Standardized testing schedules for final exams

explanation: Correct! The physical environment is all about tangible surroundings like clean toilets, solid buildings, and safe drinking water. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h2)

question: A student has stomach cramps and diarrhea after drinking from the school tap. Which part of the school environment failed here?
explanation: Well done! Safe drinking water is a basic part of the physical school environment, so bad water means a breakdown in physical safety. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is a main duty of a nurse working in a school?

options.A: Purchasing food supplies for the school cafeteria
options.B: Conducting routine health screenings and managing minor injuries
options.C: Setting the financial budget for local education ministries
options.D: Designing the structural blueprints for new school buildings

explanation: Exactly! School nurses focus on first aid, checking students' health, and handling everyday health needs right on campus. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h3)

question: A school nurse notices several students rubbing their eyes and squinting at the chalkboard. What should she do?
explanation: You nailed it! Squinting at the board is a classic sign of eye trouble, so a quick vision check is the best next step. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of health education in schools?

options.A: To help students adopt and maintain healthy lifestyle behaviors
options.B: To train students to administer prescription drugs
options.C: To replace traditional biology and science classes
options.D: To diagnose complex medical disorders in children

explanation: Correct! Health education is all about giving students practical knowledge to build good, lifelong personal habits. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why must health education topics change as children grow older?

options.A: Because older students refuse to study basic hygiene practices
options.B: To ensure teachers do not repeat the exact same lesson plan
options.C: To match the developmental stage and emerging life challenges of the students
options.D: Because younger children cannot understand the human body

explanation: Spot on! Topics like personal growth or reproductive health need to be introduced at the right age so students can truly relate to and apply them. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is a major effect of malnutrition in school children?

options.A: Impaired learning capacity and weakened immunity
options.B: Enhanced resistance to common viral infections
options.C: Rapid acceleration in physical height and bone density
options.D: Increased ability to focus for long hours

explanation: That's right! Without proper nutrients, the body and brain struggle, leading to poor concentration, tiredness, and frequent sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h5)

question: Students vomit and have stomach pain after eating snacks from an outside vendor near the gate. What should be done urgently?

options.A: Increasing the academic workload to distract students from illness
options.B: Replacing all classroom desks and chairs with new furniture
options.C: Inspecting and regulating food hygiene practices around the school
options.D: Canceling all physical education classes for the remainder of the term

explanation: Great job! Food poisoning from external sellers means health authorities need to step in and check food safety standards fast. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which health benefit comes directly from regular physical education in schools?

options.A: Prevention of childhood obesity and improved motor skills
options.B: Immediate cure for congenital heart defects
options.D: Complete elimination of infectious respiratory diseases

explanation: Correct! Staying active helps kids burn energy, build strong bones and muscles, and improve their coordination. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why are recreational play breaks important alongside structured classroom lessons?

options.A: They allow teachers to grade papers without student interruptions
options.B: They provide a necessary mental break to refresh student focus
options.C: They ensure students never feel tired during school hours
options.D: They completely replace the need for physical education curricula

explanation: Brief periods of unstructured play reduce mental fatigue, helping students return to class more attentive and ready to learn. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is a common source of emotional stress for school-aged children?
explanation: Spot on! Hard schoolwork and issues with classmates are major stressors that can weigh heavily on a child's mental health. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why is it important for a school counseling service to be confidential?

options.A: It guarantees that parents will never be informed of any school issues
options.B: It encourages students to seek help without fear of stigma or punishment
options.C: It allows the school to hide student disciplinary records from the public
options.D: It replaces the need for academic tutoring in difficult subjects

explanation: Well done! Confidentiality creates trust, making students feel safe enough to share their worries without fear of being judged. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a school health programme?

options.A: To eliminate the need for community health workers
options.B: To penalize teachers whose classes have poor attendance records
options.C: To measure success, identify gaps, and improve service delivery
options.D: To calculate the exact financial profits of the school canteen

explanation: Correct! Checking in on the programme helps us see what is working well and fix areas that need more attention. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h8)

question: A school clinic notices a sudden jump in waterborne infections among students. What should the team do next?

options.A: Close the school permanently without further investigation
options.B: Increase the academic passing grade for science examinations
options.C: Punish the students for failing to wash their hands at home
options.D: Investigate the water source and sanitation facilities for contamination

explanation: You nailed it! A spike in water illnesses points straight to a sanitation or water safety problem that needs an immediate check. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h8)
